sources.citation: Grierson, G. A. (ed.) [vol. prepared by Sten Konow]. 1905. Linguistic Survey of India, Vol. VII: Indo-Aryan Family, Southern Group: Specimens of the Marathi Language. Calcutta: Office of the Superintendent of Government Printing. 'Nahari' section pp. 379-386 (remarks p. 379; specimens pp. 379-386).
sources.note: Silent on stress/accent. The only phonetic remark is 'The phonetical system is the same as in Hal'bi' (p. 379); the rest of the page is on case suffixes, pronouns and verb forms, followed by two specimens (Kanker). No acute accents are used in the Nahari transliteration, although the volume's preface reserves the acute for marking accented syllables 'when it is necessary'.

sources.citation: Grierson, G. A. (ed.). 1905. LSI Vol. VII, 'Hal'bi' section pp. 329-378, 'Pronunciation' pp. 331-332 (the phonetic system Nahari is said to share).
sources.note: Silent on stress: the Pronunciation paragraphs treat vowel interchange (a/o, ai/ui), anunasika, palatals, cerebral d/r, cerebral n > dental, l/r, b for Marathi v, sh > kh, faint initial h; no mention of accent or stress. The whole volume's 'accent'/'stress' hits are only in the preface's transliteration note and in the Konkani and Sarasvat-Konkani sections, not in Halbi/Nahari.
